title: Manchester Museum and Science Gallery Bengaluru Sign MoU to Build Youth Learning and Nature Programmes
summary: The two institutions will create mentorship and learning programmes for young people and link biodiversity research with public engagement.
body_html:
Bengaluru, 26 October 2026: Manchester Museum, part of The University of Manchester, and Science Gallery Bengaluru have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to create new opportunities for young people and to work together on biodiversity and nature.

Under the partnership, Manchester Museum will draw on Science Gallery Bengaluru's work with students, especially its Mentorship Initiative, to build programmes for young people focused on learning, mentorship and creative career pathways.

Science Gallery Bengaluru's Nature Lab, part of its Public Lab Complex, will collaborate with Manchester Museum's conservation work. The aim is to act as a two-way bridge between biodiversity research and public engagement in both cities.

"Bengaluru is a city driven by creativity and innovation, where there's a tangible sense of care for the natural world and a commitment to creating opportunities for future generations," said Esme Ward, Director of Manchester Museum. "Science Gallery Bengaluru does an incredible job of inspiring young people and we're excited to build on that."

Dr Jahnavi Phalkey, Director of Science Gallery Bengaluru, said: "At Science Gallery Bengaluru, we value research-based engagement and new ways of bringing science to the public. We are delighted to collaborate with Manchester Museum and explore how our two institutions can learn from each other."

The MoU was signed at Science Gallery Bengaluru during the Greater Manchester Mission to India, in the presence of Professor Duncan Ivison, President and Vice-Chancellor of The University of Manchester, and Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester.

During the mission, The University of Manchester also announced plans for a new centre in Bengaluru focused on education, research and innovation, which is intended to create opportunities for students and researchers in India.
